name: RNO-G
summary: RNO-G is a radio-neutrino observatory in the Greenland ice at Summit Station. Its dark-matter role derives from ultrahigh-energy neutrino physics and future model tests.
detection_principle: Detects Askaryan radio pulses from neutrino-induced cascades in ice. Deep phased-array triggering and shallow antennas jointly reconstruct directions and reject surface backgrounds.

results.summary: Studies cosmic-ray, solar-flare, aircraft and other backgrounds, alongside full-array neutrino searches; no dark-matter discovery claimed.
Model studies forecast RNO-G constraints on ultrahigh-energy neutrinos from heavy dark-matter decay.

science_scope: Searches cosmic gamma-ray, antiparticle or neutrino spectra, directions and fluxes for indirect signatures of dark-matter annihilation, decay or related new physics. Conventional astrophysical sources and propagation can produce similar signals, requiring background modeling; design sensitivity is not a measured limit or discovery.
